children: The Japanese yen could fall further following a media report that Japan's government is considering a supplementary budget, MUFG Bank's Derek Halpenny says in a note. The potential budget, reported by the Yomiuri newspaper, could rekindle doubts over the government's push toward fiscal consolidation, he says. It could lead to a renewed widening between short and long-term Japanese government bond yields which tends to coincide with yen underperformance, he says. "Even if small in size it could still blur the lines on the government and the Bank of Japan being in unison in fighting inflation risks." The dollar rises 0.1% to 158.18 yen after reaching a near two-week high of 158.50 overnight, LSEG data show. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
